pros: Databases switch between table, board, calendar and gallery views
Relations and rollups link tasks, projects and clients without spreadsheets
Workspace Q&A answers questions with citations to source pages
Any page publishes to the web in one click
Free plan is enough for individual use
cons: No enforced structure, so workspaces sprawl without an owner
Large databases with many rollups load slowly
Offline support is partial and mobile editing lags desktop
Full AI usage requires a paid plan
verdict_line: Pick Notion if you want docs, wiki and project databases in one workspace with AI answers over all of it.

pros: Transcript appears live during the call, not after processing
Mobile app records in-person meetings as well as video calls
Entry paid plan is cheaper than most competitors
Audio is synced to text so clicking a sentence plays it
Summaries are short and action items name the right people
cons: CRM and project tool integrations are thin
Strong only in English; mixed language meetings handled poorly
Bot joins every calendar meeting by default unless changed
Retention and data residency controls lag enterprise expectations
verdict_line: Pick Otter if you want live transcripts and cheap summaries for yourself or a small team without CRM sync.

pros: CRM syncs attach notes to the right contact and deal
Search filters every past call by speaker, topic or keyword
Transcribes dozens of languages for international teams
Summary templates differ per meeting type
API and webhooks push transcripts into internal systems
cons: Speaker labels drift on calls with more than four people
Action items include topics merely discussed, not agreed
Free plan AI summary limits make it mainly a trial
Interface surfaces many features at once and feels busy
verdict_line: Pick Fireflies if meeting notes must land in Salesforce, HubSpot or your task tracker without manual copying.

pros: App library covers thousands of tools with vendor maintained connectors
Every step tests against real sample data before going live
Run history shows data per step and failed runs replay
AI step classifies, summarises and extracts inside normal Zaps
Handles authentication, rate limits and retries for you
cons: Task based pricing climbs fast on busy triggers
Polling triggers add minutes of delay on lower plans
Complex branching Zaps are hard to debug with little versioning
Tables, Interfaces and Agents are immature next to dedicated tools
verdict_line: Pick Zapier if you need two SaaS tools connected this week without an engineer.
